 DBKL To Brief Anwar On Kuala Lumpur Flood Mitigation Ahead Of Monsoon
 By Business Today Editorial 
 November 16, 2026 
 Share 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin 
 Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has been asked to brief Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on its flood mitigation measures and governance practices ahead of the Northeast Monsoon and a possible Super El Niño phenomenon next year.
 Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the number of flash flood hotspots in the capital had fallen from 31 in 2022 to 14 this year, with DBKL aiming to reduce it to 10 by year-end. 
 She said DBKL branch offices in all Kuala Lumpur parliamentary constituencies were required to report directly to the mayor whenever rainfall occurred, allowing agencies to coordinate their response promptly.
 Two task forces have also been established to strengthen flood mitigation efforts and develop open spaces that can absorb rainwater under the sponge city concept.
 Hannah said 4,162 personnel from various Federal Territories agencies were on standby, supported by 139 lorries, 60 boats and 144 four-wheel-drive vehicles. A total of 120 temporary relief centres had also been prepared, with capacity for up to 31,000 flood victims.
 Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL had allocated RM27 million next year to continue reducing flood hotspots to 10 or fewer.
 Maintenance of drainage systems, rivers and retention ponds has been increased from twice a year to quarterly, with work scheduled every two months during the monsoon season. Seven contractors are responsible for drainage systems while another 12 maintain retention ponds.
 Additional measures include modifying roadside drainage inlets, deploying 180-horsepower pumps at 10 low-lying locations and expanding the city’s on-site detention infrastructure.
 DBKL has completed nine on-site detention ponds, is constructing six more and plans to build another six in 2027. It is also monitoring more than 65 privately developed ponds and has completed a 1.3km flood barrier.
 Fadlun said DBKL had activated an operations room to monitor weather conditions, obtain forecasts one to two hours ahead, coordinate responses and issue early warnings to residents in flood-prone areas.
